source: Published patent applications reviewed as directional evidence of competitor technical and workflow investment
methodology: Records are filtered by publication date because that is when an application becomes publicly observable. Analyst implications describe possible roadmap relevance and do not assert product availability, claim scope, validity, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: Silicon-coated ion-source flow path for mass spectrometry
insights.signal: The published application describes an ion-source flow path with a silicon or silicon-hydride coating and a hydrogen carrier-gas method for ionizing and analyzing a sample by mass.
insights.roadmapImplication: Use this family as a prompt to compare source-path inertness, contamination control, maintenance burden, and analytical robustness across relevant Waters and Agilent MS workflows.
insights.watchNext: Implementation in commercial Agilent ion sources, application notes that connect the coating to reduced adsorption or maintenance, and controlled comparative evidence on sensitivity and uptime.
insights.evidenceBoundary: This family was granted in the United Kingdom in 2026, but the record does not establish implementation in a current product, LC-MS applicability, commercial performance, or freedom to operate.

insights.title: HPLC/MS monitoring of lipid stability in mRNA-loaded lipid nanoparticles
insights.signal: The published application describes an HPLC/MS apparatus and method for identifying and measuring lipid components in mRNA-loaded LNPs across storage and formulation conditions, including lyophilized and non-lyophilized samples.
insights.roadmapImplication: Evaluate whether Next Gen LC needs an LNP stability workflow package that connects separation, accurate-mass confirmation, calibration, sample preparation, and formulation-study reporting.
insights.watchNext: National-stage claims, an Agilent application note or launch using the workflow, and customer evidence that LNP stability monitoring is a buying criterion rather than a specialist method.
insights.evidenceBoundary: A pending application indicates an attempted area of protection. It does not establish granted claim scope, commercial availability, performance superiority, or customer adoption.

insights.title: Collision-cross-section-guided precursor selection for DDA mass spectrometry
insights.signal: The published application uses a collision-cross-section indicator to select or order DDA precursor targets and may adapt fragmentation energy or method, with explicit relevance to modified or cross-linked peptides and proteins.
insights.roadmapImplication: Pressure-test whether Waters acquisition workflows make precursor prioritization and fragmentation decisions equally transparent, reproducible, and useful for complex biopharma characterization.
insights.watchNext: Continuation filings, implementation in Orbitrap or multi-reflection TOF workflows, software-release notes, and comparative evidence on identification depth, duty cycle, and reproducibility.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The application describes proposed methods and possible analyzer implementations. It does not prove that a current Thermo Fisher product uses the claims or delivers a measured customer outcome.

insights.title: Peak tracking across liquid-chromatography conditions using molecular-weight correspondence
insights.signal: The application describes matching chromatographic peaks across different analysis conditions by calculating molecular weights from mass-to-charge data, reducing reliance on an unchanged mass-spectrum pattern during method development.
insights.roadmapImplication: Treat cross-condition peak correspondence as a workflow requirement for method scouting: assess whether Waters can shorten review time while preserving traceability when retention and spectral patterns shift.
insights.watchNext: US-family prosecution, software or method-development releases, supported detector combinations, and user evidence on reduced manual peak reconciliation.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The English abstract is a machine translation of a pending Japanese application. No claim is made about final scope, implementation quality, or availability in a Shimadzu product.

insights.title: Lower-complexity retention-time alignment for separation-coupled mass spectrometry
insights.signal: The application divides retention-time and mass-spectral data into m/z sub-ranges and independently aligns chromatographic peaks within those subsets to reduce data complexity across experiments.
insights.roadmapImplication: Evaluate run-to-run alignment as part of the end-to-end LC-MS workflow, including how Waters handles component-level retention shifts without obscuring data provenance or forcing excessive manual review.
insights.watchNext: SCIEX OS release notes, proteomics or small-molecule workflows using the method, prosecution changes, and benchmark evidence for alignment accuracy and processing time.
insights.evidenceBoundary: The assignee is a SCIEX operating-company entity, and the record is a pending application. The filing does not establish that the method is shipping, exclusive, valid, or superior.
